findings.quote: No method a student would use lands on this option; it is a filler value.
findings.note: Option 2 is 5 m/s² and 5 m, and the standard slip of writing s = ½at instead of s = ½at² gives ½ × 5 × 2 = 5 m alongside the correct acceleration, landing exactly on it. The next entry in this same list states that very route, so the solution contradicts itself.
findings.fix: Dropping the square on the time in s = ½at² and computing ½ × 5 × 2 = 5 m, while getting the acceleration right, which gives 5 m/s² and 5 m.

notes: a = 10/2 = 5 m/s² and s = ½ × 5 × 2² = 10 m, which is also v_avg × t = 5 × 2. The distractor claims for options 3 and 4 hold: a pairwise search over v, t, a, ½at², at², ½at and v²/2a found no route to 6 m or to 6 m/s². The supporting numbers inside the entry for option 3 (5 m from dropping the square, 20 m from forgetting the half) are both correct.
